page: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory and compression performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression and single-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. However, raw computational benchmarks show some limitations, with a weak PassMark CPU score and a weak CPU encryption score. Multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and Redis SET operations perform in the average tier.

The m9g.xlarge offers an efficient ARM-based architecture that balances memory bandwidth and general compute capabilities. While it lacks advanced vector and matrix extensions and local NVMe storage, its high memory bandwidth and dedicated core allocation make it cost-efficient for workloads requiring consistent memory access without heavy cryptographic or floating-point demands. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, caching layers like Redis, database operations, and lightweight text or prompt processing.
